# Frontend Routes — Verified Inventory

**Source of truth:** `src/routeTree.gen.ts` (auto-generated by TanStack Router) and `src/routes/*`.
**Verified against:** `main` @ `c44a29a` (PR #447 merged), dev server `http://localhost:8080`, 2026-08-06.
**Router:** TanStack Start (file-based routes in `src/routes/`). Each `*.tsx` route file declares `createFileRoute("/path")` and imports its page component from the matching `-*.page.tsx` module. The `-` prefix files are plain components, **not** routes.

## 404 / not-found behavior

Unknown paths (e.g. `/soak-report` at the root, or any typo) render `NotFoundComponent` in `src/routes/__root.tsx`:

> **404 — Signal not found**
> *This route is not in the engine map.*

That message is the app's "missing route" screen. It appears only for genuinely unregistered paths or when a route throws `notFound()`. As of the verified build, **every path linked from the UI resolves** — if a user sees the 404, it is either a typed/bookmarked URL that does not exist, or a stale deployed build that predates a route being registered (redeploy to fix).

## Route-file convention

- Route definition: `src/routes/<name>.tsx` → `createFileRoute("/name")`, `component: <Page>`.
- Page component: `src/routes/-<name>.page.tsx` (plain React, no router context).
- After adding/renaming a route file, the generated `src/routeTree.gen.ts` must be regenerated (dev server / build does this automatically). If a new route 404s after deploy, the route tree was likely generated against an older `src/routes/` snapshot — rebuild.

## Known non-route paths (HTTP 404 expected)

- `/soak-report` — there is no root-level soak-report route; the real one is `/admin/soak-report` (which redirects to `/admin`).
- Any path not listed above.
